items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: The decision-drop + spec-ref record which Resolution B variant was chosen and why, answer both Resolution A falsification questions, and close the live-feasibility-gate amendment with 7 live probes; no extra scope added beyond the sub-iterate's 6 ACs (one AC deliberately left unchecked with its own blocking-finding text, per the sub-iterate's own AC6).

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: No code, no API routes, no external service calls ship from this run. write_decision_drop.py's own field-length guard (500-char cap) was hit and handled correctly (moved long-form prose to a --spec-ref file) rather than worked around.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No user input, secrets, or credentials in any artifact this run touches. The run's own subject matter is a security question (envelope authenticity / prompt-content forgery) -- resolved explicitly in the ADR (document-the-risk over a nonce, per Architecture Review) rather than left implicit.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: No production code, no tests. The iterate spec's Confidence Calibration ledger (12 rows, each disposed as tested/untestable-this-run/reasoned) is this run's equivalent instrument for its own empirical claims.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: No code paths, no queries, no endpoints.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: The decision-drop JSON and its --spec-ref file follow write_decision_drop.py's own documented naming convention and F3's no-ADR-number-in-heading rule. A first draft appended a hand-numbered ADR directly to decision_log.md instead -- a violation of F3's single-serialization-point rule, caught by code-reviewer, reverted, and fixed to the correct decision-drop-only shape.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: The activation-envelope/record format is a new serialized producer/consumer boundary this decision creates (terminal helper -> UserPromptSubmit -> PreToolUse). Producer/consumer pairs and the full schema/scoping/consumption contract are named in the iterate spec's Affected Boundaries and Contract for R2 sections. No round-trip test exists yet because R0 ships no code implementing either side -- explicitly named as R2's job (blocking precondition 2) in the ADR, not silently skipped.
